gaps.description: Proposal and Quotation: This process does not currently specify what happens if a customer requests mid-negotiation changes to committed go-live dates after a proposal has already been approved at a given discount tier. In practice this is resolved ad hoc between the AE and Sales Manager; no formal escalation path exists.
gaps.suggestion: Declared by the source document itself; the fix belongs to the process owner.

gaps.description: Bug Reporting and Escalation: This process does not document what happens when a customer reports a bug on a deprecated product version that is no longer receiving active development (e.g., a legacy NexFlow configuration mode retired from new sales but still running for a small number of legacy customers). In practice, these reports are currently triaged case-by-case by the Engineering Manager with no documented standard, which has led to inconsistent customer communication in at least two known cases.
gaps.suggestion: Declared by the source document itself; the fix belongs to the process owner.

gaps.description: Customer Onboarding: This process assumes the AE's "Deal Closed" handoff record is complete. It does not specify what the Implementation Consultant should do if the handoff record is missing required fields (e.g., agreed go-live date not documented). In practice this causes kickoff delays; there is no formal fallback procedure. ---
gaps.suggestion: Declared by the source document itself; the fix belongs to the process owner.

"Onboarding" is used for two different things. HR uses "onboarding" to mean *employee* onboarding (PROC-HR-001). Implementation and Customer Success use "onboarding" to mean *customer* onboarding (PROC-IMPL-001). Always disambiguate: "employee onboarding" vs. "customer onboarding." Several older Support tickets and Slack references use bare "onboarding" and must be interpreted from context.
gaps.suggestion: Disambiguate by context (department, document) before answering.

gaps.description: "Client" vs. "Customer" vs. "Account" vs. "Customer Account." - Sales and Marketing materials predominantly say **"client."** - Customer Success and Support predominantly say **"customer."** - Finance and the billing system use **"account"** or **"customer account"** as the formal record-keeping unit (one account can technically map to multiple tenants/contracts). These are not always perfectly interchangeable — a "client" in a Sales context may refer to a prospective company before a contract exists, whereas "account" in Finance always refers to a billable, contracted entity. There is no single company-wide style guide enforcing one term; this is a long-standing, low-priority inconsistency.
gaps.suggestion: Disambiguate by context (department, document) before answering.
